questions.q: Distinguish between the Himalayan and Peninsular river systems of India.
answer: Indian rivers fall into two great groups, the Himalayan and the Peninsular, which differ in several ways.

answer.text: These rivers, such as the Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra, are perennial, because they are fed both by monsoon rain and by the melting of Himalayan snow, so they flow throughout the year. They have long courses, carry out great erosion in their upper reaches, and form deep gorges, meanders and large fertile deltas as they enter the plains.

These rivers, such as the Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri and Mahanadi, are mostly seasonal and depend on rainfall, so they shrink in the dry season. They are shorter and flow in fixed, mature valleys. Most flow east into the Bay of Bengal and form deltas, while the Narmada and Tapi flow west through rift valleys into the Arabian Sea, forming estuaries.

answer: Thus the two systems differ in water supply, age and course.
